content: Central DuPage Hospital, commonly referred to as CDH, is an independent hospital system situated across DuPage County, Illinois, in the United States. Its main facility is a 361-bed hospital located in Winfield, Illinois. Additionally, the hospital system includes twenty primary care facilities distributed throughout the county and four retirement communities. Central DuPage Hospital holds the distinction of being the first hospital in DuPage County to perform open-heart surgery and is currently recognized as the second busiest surgical center in the state of Illinois. The Central DuPage Hospital Association was founded in 1958 when residents from Glen Ellyn, Lombard, Wheaton, Warrenville, Winfield, and West Chicago collaborated to restore a sanitarium located on the site where the hospital's primary facility now stands. Following an extensive renovation project costing over a million dollars, Central DuPage Hospital officially opened its doors on September 16, 1964, with a capacity of 113 beds and a medical staff of 66 physicians. The hospital underwent significant expansion during the 1970s, including the opening of a 120-bed pavilion on December 13, 1970, smaller additions in 1971 and 1972, and the construction of a five-story patient tower with 112 beds in 1976. In July 2007, Central DuPage Hospital in Winfield, Illinois, announced its plans to collaborate with ProCure Treatment Centers Inc. and Radiation Oncology Consultants, Ltd. to introduce advanced cancer treatment options to the state of Illinois. The hospital projected that patient treatment utilizing these new cancer therapies would commence by 2010.
